This regular second appeal is filed by the appellant challenging the judgment and decree dated 27.06.2011, passed in R.A.No.70/2009 by the learned Additional Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) & JMFC,
Tumkur, and the judgment and decree dated 22.06.2009, passed in O.S.No.419/1997 by the learned II Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.), Tumkur.
2. For convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the trial Court.
The appellant is the defendant, and the respondent is the plaintiff.

3. The brief facts leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
The plaintiff filed a suit for permanent injunction restraining the defendant from interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the plaint schedule property.
It is the case of the plaintiff, the plaintiff is the owner in possession and enjoyment of land converted into non- agricultural purpose.
For valuable consideration, the plaintiff purchased the plaint schedule land from one Nagaraju under the registered sale deed dated 08.01.1986.
The name of the plaintiff was entered in the revenue records.

The plaintiff applied for permission from the Deputy Commissioner to convert agricultural lands into non-agriculture on 05.07.1994 and also applied for permission to make a layout by forming sites on the plaint schedule land.
The Hirehally Mandal Panchayat transferred the khatha in the plaintiff's name, and the Deputy Commissioner passed an order to convert agricultural land into non-agriculture.
The defendant has no right, title or interest over the suit schedule property.
The defendant tried trespassing into the plaint schedule property, obstructing the plaintiff and his men from demarcating and measuring the land for forming sites.
Hence, a cause of action arose for the plaintiff to file the suit for permanent injunction.

4. The defendant filed a written statement denying the averments made in the plaint and contended that the plaintiff suppressed the fact that the defendant was in possession of the plaint schedule land, and the conversion order was cancelled as per the entry in RTC.

It is denied that the plaintiff had purchased the plaint schedule land from one Nagaraju under the registered sale deed dated Gangahanumaiah S/O Hanumaiah vs B K Nanjappa S/O Kenchaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165927733/

sentences.text: It is contended that as of the date of registration of the sale deed, the vendor of the plaintiff was no longer the owner as per the decree passed in O.S.No.19/1986, vide judgment dated 15.04.1986.

It is contended that the plaintiff presented the alleged sale deed on 08.01.1986 for registration, and it was registered on 16.02.1991, as the said sale deed was kept pending for want of sufficient stamp.
It is contended that the plaintiff has managed to get the alleged sale deed through the District Registrar on 16.02.1991.
It is contended that this Court registered the sale deed on 16.06.1989, under the decree in O.S.No.232/1983, against Ramakka and her sons, and the plaintiff's name was also entered in the records.

The plaintiff filed a suit against Ramakka and her sons in O.S.No.87/1987 on the file of learned Principal Civil Judge, Tumkur, alleged to have executed two agreements of sale dated 25.06.1982 and 17.07.1984 by them.
In the said suit, the plaintiff filed an interlocutory application for impleading his vendor S.B.Nagaraju as a defendant and for adjudicating the rights of the parties.
The defendant was also impleaded in the said suit as defendant No.6.
The Court has dismissed I.A.No.6, and the said order was not challenged, and the plaintiff has withdrawn the suit on 29.10.1990.
The plaintiff has not acquired any title by virtue of the registered sale deed dated 16.02.1991.
It is contended that the order of conversion was set aside by the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal in Appeal No.249/1994 vide order dated 15.02.1996.
The order passed by the KAT was challenged by the plaintiff in W.P.No.24521/1996.
The Hon'ble High Court passed an interim order of stay on 29.08.1996.
Meanwhile, the Deputy Commissioner implemented the order passed by the KAT and cancelled the conversion order.

It is contended that the defendant had purchased the land measuring 50 x 40 feet, excluding the NH-4 margin from Smt. Ramakka and her sons, by an agreement of sale dated 16.11.1980, have delivered the possession of the property in part performance of a contract.
The defendant filed a suit for the specific performance of a contract in O.S.No.232/1983, which was decreed on 29.10.1985.
During the pendency of the suit, Ramakka and her sons requested the Tahsildar to change the khatha in favour of S.B.Nagaraju.
It is contended that on the basis of the decree and sale deed, the defendant acquired right in respect of the portion of land measuring 50 x 40 feet, excluding NH-4 margin.
It is contended that the defendant is the owner of the agricultural land, including the site, which measures 50 x 40 feet.
At the plaintiff's instance, the Tahsildar, Tumkur, was ordered to evict the defendant from Sy. No. 10 and demolish the cattle shed without adopting the proper procedure established under the law.

The defendant challenged the validity and legality of the eviction order in W.P.No.19908/1989, which was allowed vide order dated 25.06.1990, and he has also filed suit for recovery of damages in O.S.No.57/1991.
The Civil Court dismissed the suit.
The defendant preferred an appeal in R.A.No.14/1994, which is pending consideration.
It is contended that the defendant filed a writ petition in W.P.No.20656/1992 and also filed a writ petition in W.P.No.21906/1994.
On these grounds, sought for dismissal of the suit.

5. The Trial Court, based on the above said pleadings, framed the following issues:
(1) Whether the plaintiff proves that the plaintiff is the lawful owner in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as of the date of the suit?
(2) Whether the plaintiff further proves that the defendant has illegally attempted to trespass on the suit schedule property?

(3)To what order the parties are entitled?
6. To prove the plaintiff's case, the plaintiff examined himself as PW-1 and marked 17 documents as Exs.P1 to P17.
In rebuttal, the defendant examined himself as DW-1 and marked 29 documents as Exs.D1 to D29.
The trial Court, after assessing the oral and documentary evidence of the parties,
answered issues Nos.1 and 2 in the affirmative, issue No.3 as per the final order.
The suit of the plaintiff was decreed.
A decree for permanent injunction was granted restraining the defendant from interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
7. The defendant, aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in the above-said suit, filed an appeal in R.A.No.70/2009.

The First Appellate Court, framed the following points for consideration:
(1)Whether plaintiff proves his possession over the suit property as on the date of suit?
(2) Whether plaintiff proves the interference by defendant?
(3)Whether plaintiff is entitled for the reliefs?
(4)Whether the judgment and decree is capricious and arbitrary?

(5)Whether the appellant shows that he is entitled for production of additional evidence?
(6) What order?
8.

The First Appellate Court, after hearing the learned counsel for the parties and on re-assessing the oral and documentary evidence, answered point Nos.1 to 3 in the affirmative; point Nos.4 and 5 in the negative and consequently dismissed the appeal filed by the defendant, vide judgment dated 27.06.2011, and confirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.
The defendant, aggrieved by the judgments and decrees passed by the courts below, filed this second appeal.

9. This court admitted the appeal on 10.11.2011 to consider the following substantial question of law :
(1) In the light of the long-drawn litigation between the parties, in which the title of the plaintiff in respect of the suit schedule property had been disputed, whether a mere suit for the relief of permanent injunction in respect of the suit schedule property is maintainable in the absence of prayer for declaration of title and whether the courts below are justified in law in granting the relief of permanent injunction in favour of the respondent/plaintiff in the absence of a prayer for declaration?

It was made clear that just as any other document, the document compulsorily registered was to operate as a valid, effective document between the parties from the date on when it was executed.
"10. It is well settled that when a document is duly presented for registration (within the time prescribed), if its registration is refused or if its registration is kept pending,
and thereafter the document is registered either on the direction of the Registrar or competent Court or on the sub-Registrar satisfying himself that there is no impediment for registration
, the registered document will operate, not from the date of actual registration, but from the date when the deed was executed.
Gangahanumaiah S/O Hanumaiah vs B K Nanjappa S/O Kenchaiah on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165927733/
14 26.
Considering the law laid down by this court's Division bench, the date of presentation of the sale deed is to be considered and not the date of registration.
The sale deed cannot be invalid as of the date of passing the judgment in O.S.No.19/1986.
Considering the material on record, both the courts below were justified in entertaining the suit for permanent injunction and in the absence of prayer for declaration of title.
